_about: Vyta scorecard settings. Built from vyta_scorecard_v2.xlsx (9 Oct 2026). score.py reads this file - change thresholds, weights and bands here, no code changes needed.
_how_to_edit: direction 'higher_is_worse': Amber when value >= amber, Red when value >= red.
direction 'lower_is_worse': Amber when value <= amber, Red when value <= red.
Weights within each score should add up to 100 (score.py warns if not).
Set "enabled": false to drop an indicator without deleting it.
Save the file, then re-run score.py. If score.py says the file is broken, check for a missing comma or quote.
disclaimer: Indicative early-warning signals only - not an insolvency determination or professional advice. Thresholds are working assumptions, not industry-calibrated benchmarks.

overrides.reason: An unpaid statutory demand is a formal insolvency trigger.
Trading has collapsed or the books have stopped, while short-term debts exceed short-term assets (or the business owes more than it owns).

Low.Uncertain: Performance review: margin, pricing and overhead improvements.
Low.Weak: Structural concern: fix the business model before cash runs out.

Moderate.Strong: Early intervention: working capital fix, refinance, ATO payment plan.
Moderate.Uncertain: Turnaround review: where has the cash been going?
Moderate.Weak: Serious: restructure or plan an orderly exit.

High.Strong: RESTRUCTURE CANDIDATE: SBR, VA or safe harbour. Profitable business with legacy balance sheet issues. Priority lead for advisory firms.
High.Uncertain: Urgent advice: assess restructure vs liquidation.
High.Weak: Likely liquidation / exit pathway (CVL, sale of business).

data_confidence._about: How much to trust the scores, based on how many of the last 12 months had trading activity.

indicators.name: Current ratio
indicators.calculation: Current assets / current liabilities (latest month-end)

indicators.name: Quick ratio
indicators.calculation: (Cash + trade debtors) / current liabilities (latest month-end)

indicators.name: Cash runway (months)
indicators.calculation: Cash / average monthly net cash outflow (last 3 months)

indicators.name: ATO debt: consecutive months rising
indicators.calculation: Count of consecutive month-ends (ending at the latest month) where total ATO liabilities increased

indicators.name: Bank debt growth (6 months)
indicators.calculation: % change in loans + overdraft balances over 6 months

indicators.name: Facility utilisation
indicators.calculation: Overdraft/facility drawn / approved limit
indicators.needs_owner_input: Approved overdraft/facility limit (not held in Xero)

indicators.name: Trade creditor days
indicators.calculation: Trade payables / (COGS + operating expenses, annualised) x 365

indicators.name: Trade creditors >90 days overdue
indicators.calculation: Unpaid bills more than 90 days past due / total unpaid bills

indicators.name: Debtor days trend (3 months)
indicators.calculation: Debtor days now minus debtor days 3 months ago. Debtor days = trade debtors / (that month's revenue x 12) x 365

indicators.name: Debtors >90 days overdue
indicators.calculation: Unpaid sales invoices more than 90 days past due / total unpaid sales invoices

indicators.name: Sales up, cash down
indicators.calculation: Consecutive months (ending at the latest month) where rolling 3-month revenue rose and the cash balance fell

indicators.name: Operating cash flow ratio
indicators.calculation: Operating cash flow (last 12 months) / current liabilities. Operating cash flow estimated as net profit + depreciation - increase in debtors + increase in creditors and ATO liabilities

indicators.name: Debt-to-asset ratio
indicators.calculation: Total liabilities / total assets

indicators.name: Sales against a normal month
indicators.calculation: Latest month's sales / average monthly sales over the 12 months before it
indicators.status: New Oct 2026: closed-job benchmark (sales collapse before appointment)

indicators.name: Books kept up to date
indicators.calculation: Months in a row (to the latest) where sales + costs recorded are under 5% of a normal month (average of the last 12 active months). Also Amber when total liabilities are below zero (liability accounts in debit)
indicators.status: New Oct 2026: closed-job benchmark (ASIC v Plymin: can't produce timely, accurate financial information)

indicators.name: Equity ratio
indicators.calculation: Net assets / total assets

indicators.name: Gross margin
indicators.calculation: Gross profit / revenue (last 12 months)

indicators.name: Gross margin trend (12 months)
indicators.calculation: Gross margin (last 12 months) minus gross margin (previous 12 months), in percentage points

indicators.name: Overhead / gross profit
indicators.calculation: Operating expenses / gross profit (last 12 months)

indicators.name: Underlying profit margin
indicators.calculation: (Net profit + interest + depreciation + one-off/legacy costs) / revenue (last 12 months)
indicators.needs_owner_input: One-off/legacy costs to add back (optional; defaults to $0)

indicators.name: Revenue trend (12 months)
indicators.calculation: % change in rolling 12-month revenue vs the previous 12 months

indicators.name: Pipeline coverage
indicators.calculation: Open quotes value / average monthly revenue
indicators.needs_data: Xero Quotes - not currently pulled by pull_data.py

indicators.name: Long-term asset coverage
indicators.calculation: Non-current assets / non-current liabilities

owner_questions.question: Has the business received a statutory demand (or legal letter of demand) in the last 6 months?
Is the business behind on any bank loan repayments, or has the bank extended or increased limits recently?
Is there an ATO payment plan in place, and is it being met?
Who is your customer, and what problem do you solve for them?
What is your sustainable competitive advantage? If you don't have one, could you get one?
If the cash problem were fixed tomorrow, would the business make money? Why?
Where has the cash been going over the last 12 months?
Could the business operate with a smaller overhead? What would you cut?
What does the pipeline, work in progress or order book look like for the next 3 months?
Is the business capital-intensive with thin margins, or carrying a large fixed overhead?
